To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the numerical methods used to study astrophysical and cosmological problems are conditionally stable and that the conversion of conditionally-stable methods into unconditionally stable methods enhances the robustness and the range of applicability of numerical methods considerably.
the numerical solution of the Boltzmann equation is feasible and that this method is a promising candidate for the solution of the Boltmann equation in astrophysical and cosmological problems.

(1) the conversion from a conditionally-stable to a time-explicit unconditionally-stable scheme is a powerful method to enhance the robust and unification of a numerical method, (2) the conversion of the time-implicit to the time-explicit method can be done for any type of numerical scheme, and (3) the time-explicit M1 solver is a very promising tool for the simulation of MHD turbulence and the study of the evolution of molecular clouds and the interstellar medium
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of numerical algorithms for the solution of hyperbolic partial differential equations, which are applicable to a wide range of problems in astrophysics.
the numerical solution of hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs) in astrophysical and cosmological applications, and the development of robust, unconditionally-stable numerical algorithms.
the development and application of robust, unconditionally stable, high-resolution numerical methods for the solution of astrophysical fluid dynamic problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
computational gas dynamics has become the most important tool in the investigation of the physics of astrophysical fluid flows.
the conversion of time-explicit numerical schemes is a very promising strategy to improve their applicability in astrophysical gas dynamics.

numerical methods in astropysics and cosmology have come of age and have reached a stage where they are able to provide accurate and reliable solutions of the underlying partial differential equations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a robust, unconditionally stable numerical scheme for solving the Boltzmann equation in the presence of magnetic fields.
we have developed and implemented a new numerical method for the time-explicit solution of the MHD-Boltzmann equation.

we are able to compute the evolution of the magnetized interstellar medium in a self-consistent way, i.e., the gas is treated on the level of a Boltzmann equation, and the magnetic field on the level of an ideal MHD approximation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conversion of numerical methods is possible, and that it can lead to significant improvements.
the combination of time-explicit methods with a time-implicit treatment of the hyperbolic terms of the equations of motion is an efficient and robust numerical approach.

a combination of a conservative, time-explicit and unconditionally stable MHD scheme with a time-implicit, conservative and unconditionally stable solver for the Boltzmann equation can be used to simulate the evolution of a magnetized, compressible and collisional plasma.
